items.title: Steam Introduces New Age Verification Rules, Requiring a Credit Card to Purchase PC Games Such as Cyberpunk 2077 and Resident Evil Requiem
items.summary: The measure was implemented in only one country to comply with a new local law, but affected users are expressing frustration with Valve
items.content:
Steam is arguably the most widely used PC gaming platform in the world, thanks to its frequent sales and promotions. Like any major storefront, however, it must adapt to the legal regulations of each country in which it operates. Unfortunately, new age restrictions have now been introduced, and many players have already been affected.

These measures were imposed in only one country, following a new law that took effect this year. The issue is that users in that region must now verify their age if they wish to purchase some of the market’s most popular releases, and doing so requires a valid credit card.

Users in Mexico, the rest of Latin America, the United States, and other countries can breathe easy. This new requirement applies only to Australia, and for now, it seems Valve has no plans to implement similar rules in other territories.

The new guidelines stem from the Online Safety Act 2021, which mandates that all video game platforms require users to prove they are over 18 years old in order to access titles rated R18+ or MA15+ by the country’s Classification Board.

The law officially took effect in March of this year, and Valve has finally made the corresponding changes to Steam. Players residing in Australia must now confirm they are old enough to access the store pages of highly popular titles such as The Last of Us Part II, Resident Evil Requiem, and Cyberpunk 2077.

It is easy to understand why the Online Safety Act has generated considerable controversy in the United Kingdom and Australia, as many nations require users to submit photographs or other biometric data to verify they are over 18. To avoid any controversy, Valve opted for a different approach.

Specifically, Steam currently offers only one method of age verification: linking a credit card to the account. However, this comes with its own set of drawbacks, and the community has already voiced its disappointment and concern across the Internet.

While some users reported being able to satisfy the requirement by linking a debit card or even a PayPal account, it appears that the only reliable solution is to follow Valve’s instructions and use a credit card.

Users who fail to verify their age will encounter the following warning message when attempting to access certain games:

“Valve is required by the Age-Restricted Material App Distribution Services Code to verify that you are 18 or older before accessing mature content. If you wish to do so, please add a valid Australian credit card to your account and afterwards update the Mature Content Preferences.”

The problem is that many players residing in Australia do not have a credit card for one reason or another. The company also appears to disregard account longevity, as numerous users report that the platform restricted their access despite having created their Steam profiles more than 20 years ago.

“I am 43 years old and my Steam account dates back to its earliest days,” one person commented on social media. “So basically, I can’t view certain games on my 22-year-old account because I’m financially stable enough not to depend on a credit card?” another player remarked ironically.

According to reports, credit card adoption is not particularly widespread in Australia, unlike in the United States and other regions. It is estimated that only about half of Australian consumers own one, and such cards are even less common among young people between the ages of 18 and 24.

Despite the negative reaction from fans in that country, Valve has remained silent on the matter, and it is unknown whether the company will offer alternatives for affected users.

items.title: Blizzard isn't "trying to do the Steam or Epic Games Store thing" by putting Cyberpunk 2077 and The Witcher 3 Remastered on Battle.net, says exec
items.content:
CD Projekt Red's RPGs don't mean there's a substantial change happening

(Image credit: CD Projekt Red) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter During BlizzCon 2026 , we got confirmation that two massive games are coming to Battle.Net: The Witcher 3 Remastered and Cyberpunk 2077 . As you well know, these are CD Projekt Red releases, and they join a number of games from Bethesda and other publishers that have been added to Blizzard's platform post- Microsoft acquisition. Despite this, don't expect their respective deals to be harbingers for some grand expansion.

"We're obviously not out there trying to do the Steam or Epic Game Store thing," Andrew Guerrero, vice president of product management and global insight at Blizzard, told Polygon . "We have our audience. We have a passionate core of people that play Blizzard games and games similar to Blizzard, and if something makes sense for them, we'll get after it."

Sure enough, Cyberpunk 2077 and The Witcher 3 have clear overlap with the Blizzard fanbase, being large RPGs you can pour hundreds of hours into. The likes of Doom: The Dark Ages, The Outer Worlds 2 and Destiny 2 all fit, too.

The Activision merger brought a selection of games with less obvious ties, like Crash Bandicoot and Call of Duty, but you can understand the publishing mandate. Taking on projects from a whole other publisher could be seen as testing the waters for opening the storefront, but Guerrero maintains curation is key.

"It's a much more focused approach, I'd say, of 'What do we think our players would absolutely love? What are the top-tier quality experiences out there that we might be able to get some more exposure to, and does it make sense?'" he explains.

Blizzard and CD Projekt Red team up for Diablo 4 Geralt skin and The Witcher 3 on Battle.net Upcoming CD Projekt Red games: From The Witcher 4 to Cyberpunk Orion CDPR says The Witcher 3 Remastered's physical edition details will come "when the time is right" Of course, there are enormous drawbacks to even humoring becoming the kind of market Steam and the Epic Games Store offer. You have large-scale moderation, a huge increase in labor behind-the-scenes, and the uphill battle of trying to compete in a space with clear market leaders.

All of which is to say, I don't think we should expect Battle.Net to become a hive of indie development just yet. The Witcher 4 is probably a safe bet by now, however.

items.title: Diablo 4’s Witcher Collab Could Literally Only Work for One Class, Says CDPR
items.summary: Developers also reveal why Overwatch is collaborating with Cyberpunk: Edgerunners and not Cyberpunk 2077
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Tomas Franzese Published Sep 14, 2026, 11:30 AM EDT BlizzCon Developers also reveal why Overwatch is collaborating with Cyberpunk: Edgerunners and not Cyberpunk 2077

Image: Blizzard Entertainment Diablo 4 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap At this year's BlizzCon, Blizzard Entertainment's in-person fan event celebrating its many gaming franchises, CD Projekt Red unveiled a Geralt-themed skin coming to Diablo 4 and revealed that Cyberpunk: Edgerunners will cross over with Overwatch in 2027. While cross-game collaborations are a dime a dozen in live-service games nowadays, I was curious why CD Projekt Red and Blizzard specifically chose to make The Witcher collaboration a Barbarian skin and the Cyberpunk collaboration solely focus on Edgerunners . In an interview with Polygon, developers from both studios revealed why these decisions were made.

Image: Blizzard Entertainment For this collaboration, Geralt himself is not coming to Diablo 4 . Instead, a skin based on the character will be added for the Barbarian class. CD Projekt Red level design lead Miles Tost tells Polygon that this was the result of "a lot of back and forth on the creative side, which is challenging, but also part of the fun."

But why the Barbarian specifically? I could easily see Geralt's look working for a Paladin, or even a Rogue. Tost offered some insight as to why the collaboration went this direction.

"We landed on something super cool with the Barbarian because we see not just the whole weapons expertise — masters that achieve perfection through massive amounts of training — but also relatively low level of magic use. Using physical prowess in general as their main weapon, and knowledge," Tost said. "I also like to think of the Barbarian's arsenal system as something that can harken a bit to the need for preparation that a Witcher would need to go through to find the right tool for the right cause."

Once The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt's Songs of the Past becomes available for pre-order, anyone who buys it through Battle.net will get this Geralt-themed Diablo 4 skin. Songs of the Past is slated to launch sometime in 2027, and CD Projekt Red's press release says "more is in the works" for the Diablo 4 collaboration in 2027 as well.

Image: Blizzard Entertainment Image: Blizzard Entertainment Close Image: Blizzard Entertainment Image: Blizzard Entertainment window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-1-1932582008"] = '" Image: Blizzard Entertainment Image: Blizzard Entertainment Close Image: Blizzard Entertainment Image: Blizzard Entertainment "'; Cosmetics based on David from Edgerunners and Talia from Edgerunners 2 will make their way into Blizzard's popular hero shooter. While Edgerunners is a great show that fits in with past Overwatch anime collaborations like One Punch Man , I had to ask why the team didn't look to the Cyberpunk 2077 game for the initial crossover. I'm sure players would love to look like Johnny Silverhand as they play Overwatch , but that's not planned for now.

Amelia Korzycka, CD Projekt Red's expert community and social media manager, admitted that the anime crossover makes more sense because Edgerunners 2 is about to come out , and that the companies have heard clamor for Edgerunners to come to Overwatch before.

‘We've got a lot of feedback overall. Like, when you look at social media, you see a lot of comments: Oh, it would be cool if Overwatch would do a collaboration with Cyberpunk or Edgerunners ," Korzycka explained. "And Edgerunners , I think, fits a bit better for now. We will see what the future holds, but we want to start with Edgerunners , especially [because] Edgerunners 2 is almost here, right? We have a really cool crew joining Night City’s arsenal of legends and heroes."

That said, both Korzycka and Blizzard product VP Andrew Guerrero teased that a Cyberpunk 2077- specific collab would be possible one day. "We will see. We want to introduce [ Edgerunners ] first, and we'll see what's happening next," Korzycka told Polygon, with Guerrero adding, "If players respond in a really positive way, we could always do all kinds of stuff."

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 hits Netflix on Oct. 20. This collaboration will come to Overwatch next year.

items.title: New Cyberpunk 2077 DLC Officially Confirmed For 2027
items.summary: Shocking news! Cyberpunk: Edgerunners is colliding with Overwatch—what iconic skins await? Brace yourselves!
items.content:
Cyberpunk 2077 promotional image. By Angharad Redden Published Sep 14, 2026, 6:21 AM EDT Known as 'Cyberpunk 2077's' biggest fan, Angharad is a Welsh games writer who thrives in anything related to digital storytelling. If a video game explores the intricacies and horrors of womanhood, she is there. Thanks to previous work at GAMINGbible, GameByte, The Loadout, Game Luster, Angharad has built a strong understanding of both the digital world and what fans want from it and is eager to share her thoughts and expertise with readers. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google Discover Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Whilst I try to remain unbiased in these stories, it is hard not to express my excitement over the recent news of an upcoming collaboration between Cyberpunk 2077 and another of my favorite games of all time. Although details remain scarce at this time, it is a collaboration that we all hoped for, and its 2027 release window gives us ample time to guess which iconic characters and their aesthetics will be matched together.

Yes, I am talking about the news that Cyberpunk 2077, more specifically Cyberpunk: Edgerunners , will be heading to Overwatch , the top-rated hero shooter on the market, some time in the new year. Announced at 2026's Blizzcon, which took place over the weekend, the collaboration will see Cyberpunk: Edgerunners characters receive skins in Overwatch, allowing fans to see the two franchises collide, and unfortunately, spend a whole lot of money in the process.

Overwatch Blizzard Over the years, Overwatch has collaborated with the biggest names in entertainment, including anime such as Cowboy Bepop and One Punch Man, car brands such as Porsche and even Transformers, and more recently, LE SSERAFIM, the K-Pop group which has partnered up with Overwatch on three separate occasions.

Now it seems as though Cyberpunk: Edgerunners will be getting its time in the spotlight in an upcoming collaboration, and whilst we do not know the full extent of this crossover, including how many skins will be made available, we do know that David from Cyberpunk: Edgerunners and Talia from Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 will be making an appearance. However, which Overwatch characters they will be paired with remains to be seen.

From a lore perspective, David would be best matched with Lucio, a support hero who is capable of reaching high speeds across the battlefield, much like when David uses his Sandevistan. As for Talia, we are yet to see her full abilities in action, as Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 does not air until October 2026. However, her agility, acrobatic skills and physique could suit Widow, our resident sniper.

We can also expect to see both Rebecca and Lucy from Cyberpunk: Edgerunners make an appearance, although this has not yet been confirmed. However, over on r/Overwatch , fans quickly took to the comments to share which skins they would like to see.

David Martinez from Cyberpunk Edgerunners grinning while walking. "I hope it’s not all just Edgerunners , because Johnny Silverhand x Cassidy is the easiest dunk on a collab skin of all time," one comment read. "Metal arm, big hand cannon, one of the main OGs." Whilst another suggested Sombra taking on the role of Lucy, which both having the required hacking skills, and Doomfist receiving an Adam Smasher skin courtesy of their love of, well, smashing things with their fist.

At the time of writing, no official skins other than David and Talia have been confirmed, but with it being one of the most highly anticipated crossovers in Overwatch history, Blizzard has a lot of weight on its shoulders to deliver.

items.title: Blizzard Has No Plans To Turn Battle.net Into A Steam Competitor
items.summary: Even after The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 launch, Blizzard will still be very picky about bringing third-party games to Battle.net
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Tomas Franzese Published Sep 13, 2026, 9:05 PM EDT BlizzCon Even though The Witcher 3 Remastered and Cyberpunk 2077 are coming to Battle.net, Blizzard tells Polygon not to expect a flood of third-party games

Image: Blizzard Entertainment Cyberpunk 2077 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 1 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap This article is part of a directory: BlizzCon 2026: The biggest news and reveals from Blizzard's big show Previous The new StarCraft won't be out until 2030; Blizzard explains why Next World of Warcraft Forever has native gamepad support — just don't expect WoW on consoles any time soon CD Projekt Red confirmed at BlizzCon that both The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered and Cyberpunk 2077 will come to Battle.net, Blizzard's proprietary game storefront, before the end of the year. You should expect this to kick off a large wave of third-party Battle.net launches, though, as Blizzard told Polygon it's still being very picky about what will come to the service in the future.

Battle.net predates Steam, having launched in 1997 alongside the original Diablo as a platform for player chats and listings of multiplayer servers. Over time, it became the hub for buying Blizzard (and only Blizzard) games on PC. Things stayed that way until Destiny 2 launched on the service in 2017 . In the years since, other Activision-published series like Call of Duty and Crash Bandicoot made their way to Battle.net as well.

Following Microsoft's acquisition of Activision Blizzard, Xbox Game Studios and Bethesda titles like Avowed, Sea of Thieves, The Outer Worlds 2 , and Doom: The Dark Ages also made their way to Battle.net. Now that CD Projekt Red games are coming to Battle.net, you'd be remiss not to wonder if we should expect a flood of other third-party titles to come in the future.

Despite this trend, Blizzard's Andrew Guerrero quickly made it clear during a BlizzCon interview with Polygon that Blizzard has no ambition of taking on the likes of Steam.

'We're obviously not out there trying to do the Steam or Epic Game Store thing. We really look at ourselves as, you know, we have our audience. We have a passionate core of people that play Blizzard games and games similar to Blizzard, and if something makes sense for them, we'll get after it," Guerrero explained. "It's a much more focused approach, I'd say, of 'What do we think our players would absolutely love? What are the top-tier quality experiences out there that we might be able to get some more exposure to, and does it make sense?'"

Later in the interview, I asked Guerrero about what the addition of support for third-party games entails from a development standpoint. "If you look at Steam, they spend a lot of time making a platform that is explicitly for publishing games on the platform," he responded. "We didn't really build Battle.net for that, but we did spend some time getting it to a place where it's much more straightforward, and we can do it without it being completely bespoke."

That said, Guerrero said that he doesn't think Battle.net will ever get to "a place where it's, like, hit the self-publish button, everything flows through." He sees the game curation struggles that storefronts like Steam and Epic's face, and doesn't want to put games on Battle.net that Blizzard fans won't enjoy.

"We really value our players' time and attention," he said. "They're on our platform. They're looking at games that we're showing them. We really want that to be something that we're pretty confident is going to be appealing to them. If we went super, super wide, the curation just sort of becomes its own thing, and that's just not what we're trying to be."

While I'm not sure Crash Bandicoot 4: It's About Time is very Blizzard-coded, it's easy to see how CD Projekt Red RPGs like The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and Cyberpunk 2077 better fit the bill. For now, we're in a wait-and-see state, waiting to find out how well those games do on Battle.net and want other titles Blizzard deems worthy of launching on it.

items.title: A New Cyberpunk 2077 Game Is Coming This September
YouTuber tests new Cyberpunk 2077 third-person mode and the results are outstanding
items.summary: Now THIS is what the game should have been like from the start.
items.content:
Brand new animations have been added completely separate from first person in this new Cyberpunk 2077 mode.

A brand new third person mod for Cyberpunk 2077 is making the rounds on the internet, and players are demonstrating the improvements that have come in with this new release.

Although it launched with only a first person mode, Cyberpunk 2077 players have used mods over the years to unlock the game’s camera view to play from a third-person perspective.

The results have been, let’s say, less than satisfactory . Because animations were built for first-person mode, it brings some rather funky scenes when you try to move the camera away from the player’s body.

Thankfully, you can say goodbye to nightmarish bulky arms and bizarre running poses thanks to this new mod which introduces decent third-person animations to Cyberpunk 2077 .

This new video uploaded by YouTuber BleeeGMV has proved that good third-person animations in Cyberpunk 2077 are possible, showing off a variety of different animations and movements for each action you can take.

The video starts with a jogging animation, in which the player character is running down a pavement in Night City. The animation shows the character is running in a determined way, but doesn’t look janky or awkward. Their arms go forward and backwards naturally, and it looks like a pretty decent third-person animation as a result.

The video also shows what this looks like when running up or down stairs. Pretty similar, it turns out, but there are a few subtle changes in momentum to indicate that the character is on a flight of stairs.

This then changes to a short clip of the player standing in place and looking around. Their character looks at the surroundings and turns their head in place on the spot, which is a cool detail. There are also a few additional idle animations, including one where the character raises their hand and inspects it.

Read More: Cyberpunk 2077 spiritual successor No Law absolutely blew me away at Gamescom

The video then cuts to a slow walk animation, and shows off the character with a heavy swagger as they journey through a populated area. A similar amount of care and detail is present here, too.

We then cut to a sprinting animation, which looks a lot faster than the first-person sprint. However, this may only be due to the animation and FOV change that helps the illusion that the player is running faster than they actually are.

The video ends with a demonstration of what traversal looks like in third-person, particularly when vaulting or climbing over short ledges. The character actually reaches out and pulls themselves up, and even does a Lara Croft-style handstand as they climb up.

The video does not demonstrate what combat looks like in third-person, probably because they’re unfinished and clunky to use in third-person. Mod creator CybrDrake also says that these animations are mostly complete for female V at the moment, while male V’s are not yet done.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Finally Has the Third Person Camera Mod Players Have Been Demanding
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 modders finally solved third-person the right way. Not everyone's thrilled
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Rebecca Corgan Published Sep 11, 2026, 3:30 PM EDT Culture Your custom character, finally visible

Cyberpunk 2077 is a game about a lot of things, but isolation and self-discovery are major themes. Image: CD Projekt Red via Polygon Cyberpunk 2077 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap CD Projekt Red developed Cyberpunk 2077 in first person for a specific narrative reason. Igor Sarzynski, creative director on the upcoming Cyberpunk 2 , recently laid out why the choice worked so well for the original game : V spends the story as a mind trapped in a decaying body, with Johnny Silverhand’s digital ghost inside her head, visible to no one but her. A third-person camera, Sarzynski argued, would put V and Johnny on equal footing for the viewer, instead of keeping that presence locked inside her own point of view. This is extremely valid rationale, but Cyberpunk 2077 players have long been begging for a third-person camera for an equally valid reason: The game lets you go all in on character and outfit customization, then gives you very few opportunities to see that artwork in action.

But no longer are Cyberpunk 2077 players trapped in first-person.

The Cyberpunk 2077 mod Immersive Third Person – Best of Both Worlds addresses this issue while preserving the original game’s vibe. Modder CybrDrake released this new third-person camera mod on Sept. 3. With the mod, players can toggle between full third-person movement and first-person movement as wanted or needed. It also switches automatically when it needs to — dropping back to first person for combat, cutscenes, and terminal use, then handing the view back once you're clear. The mod rebuilds V's third-person animation set from the ground up, instead of recycling existing movements. Female V is fully covered for now, with a planned update shortly incoming for male V movements. The camera free-orbits with wall collision, and the mod gives you five savable profiles to let you set camera height and distance for the various moods you want to set.

To get the mod running, you will need to accomplish a few technical tasks, like installing the various files through a mod manager (or piling them in game folders manually, if you’re so inclined), and making sure you bind a camera toggle key — a quick step, but one that’s easy to miss, and the mod won’t work until that’s set. Whether you’re familiar with mods or this is your first one, it should only take a few moments, and the install and troubleshooting instructions on the mod’s page are comprehensive.

Image: CD Projekt Red Player reception to the mod has also been comprehensive…and mixed. Some of those contributing to the discourse on X are delighted, joking that they can finally see “V the way God intended.” Others pushed back, citing CD Projekt Red’s description of the game as specifically a first-person RPG and noting — as of just a few weeks ago, on a subreddit dedicated to modding the game, that perhaps the reason no good third-person mod existed (at that point) was because Cyberpunk 2077 simply shouldn’t be played that way . (Commenters on the mod page itself mostly just want more features in the mod itself — requests that the modder seems extremely open to implementing.) The split likely comes down to the way people categorize and experience Cyberpunk 2077 : Is it a first-person shooter with RPG systems attached, or an RPG shipped in first person?

A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

The mod doesn’t touch that debate, but it lets you play whichever version you believe in. And the payoff shows up in many in-game places you might not expect. Braindance sequences read strange and a little uncanny from a new point of view, built as they are around the gap between watching a scene and inhabiting it. Delamain rides might just look better from outside the cab than from behind the wheel. And walking through Adam Smasher’s part of the story with a full view of V’s cyberware makes those upgrades feel less theoretical and more earned — a bit more of a perceived payoff for every credit you spent at a ripperdoc. While Night City was always worth dressing up for, now, with this new mod, it might finally be time to enjoy watching your character walk through it.

The owners of Cypress Cove Resort are dealing with GTA 6 pranksters

To survive in Night City, you need someone to watch your back. On the way to the major leagues, V managed to gather a remarkable crew. You could even say, a crew to remember!

items.content:
Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.

items.title: Patch 2.31
items.summary: Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live! This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below: Vehicles Updated Aut
items.content:
Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live!

This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below:

Vehicles

  • Updated AutoDrive. When driving to a selected point, the vehicle now drives smoothly, overtakes blocking vehicles and no longer stops at traffic lights. Free Roam mode has also been upgraded to follow traffic rules and navigate the city more reliably.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Johnny always spawned in the passenger seat when using the Delamain Cab service.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where applying CrystalCoat to the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru caused its wheels to flash in different colors.

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Most of the new poses introduced in Update 2.3 now work with any gender.

    [/*]

  • Disabled NPC collision, which will make it easier to position NPCs on top of other objects with collision (e.g. on car hoods).

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where some of the poses didn't work for Royce.

    [/*]

Quests & Open World

  • Freedom - Fixed the journal entry that appears when the player chooses not to steal the Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred."

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where, after V fails to pursue and stop Semimaru and receives a text from River saying he'll contact V soon, the follow-up message never arrives.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where the Yaiba Semimaru could flip over during the chase, preventing the player from entering it.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - It's no longer possible to trigger the quest if River died during The Hunt.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Players can now acquire the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru through AUTOFIXER even if they failed The Hunt, which normally unlocks the side quest where the vehicle is obtained.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed a game crash that could occur in certain circumstances after leaving the Yaiba showroom event.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed an issue where the proxy interface UI in the Yaiba showroom is cut off when the "Larger HUD Elements" setting is enabled.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Fixed several localization and lipsync issues in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle to disable vignette. It can be found in Settings → Graphics → Basic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on PC and Mac where Ray-Traced Reflections might not display correctly when enabled under certain conditions.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several issues with displaying text messages from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Various fixes for fluff vendors.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Fixed an issue where NVIDIA Reflex could be disabled while DLSS Frame Generation was enabled, causing the screen to turn pink.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Path Tracing didn't activate properly in certain scenarios.

    [/*]

Mac-specific

  • Fixed an issue where changing graphics presets on Mac set Screen Space Reflections to a higher setting compared to the equivalent presets on PC.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing a permanent white screen when Frame Generation is enabled while entering the braindance in The Information.

    [/*]

  • Selecting "Defaults" in Video Settings no longer turns HDR Mode off.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where setting the MetalFX DRS Maximum Resolution above the value applied by the “For this Mac” preset could cause visual artifacts.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the inverted behavior of the "Mute Game in Background" toggle in Settings.

    [/*]

  • Removed the outdated "(Requires Game Restart)" disclaimer from the mouseover description of the "Disable Spatial Audio" setting.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on the App Store version that caused the game to become stuck on the “Press Space to continue” breaching screen.

    [/*]

  • Various stability and performance optimizations.

    [/*]

items.title: Update 2.3 Patch Notes
items.summary: Update 2.3 lands tomorrow! Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! It also contains updates for CrystalCoat™ and Photo Mode, as well as sup
items.content:
Update 2.3 lands tomorrow!

Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! It also contains updates for CrystalCoat™ and Photo Mode, as well as support for AMD FSR 3.1 Frame Generation, Intel XeSS 2.0 and HDR10+ Gaming, among others.

Update 2.3 also brings Cyberpunk 2077 to a whole new platform: Mac with Apple silicon! If you already own the game on Steam, you can play it on your compatible device. To find out whether your Mac can run Cyberpunk 2077, please check the official requirements.

Read the list of changes for more info:

Vehicles

  • Added 4 new vehicles, including several Side Jobs tied to acquiring them:

    • Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Hunt and The Beast In Me).

      An additional side job unlocks the CrystalCoat™ feature for it.

      [/*]

    • Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred"

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Beast in Me: Badlands, The Beast in Me: Santo Domingo, Transmission, and Search and Destroy)."

      [/*]

    • Yaiba ASM-R250 Muramasa

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, purchase 1 Yaiba vehicle, purchase at least 3 vehicles through AUTOFIXER, and complete Reported Crime: You Play with Fire...).

      If you fail the side job, the vehicle can later be purchased through AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]

    • Chevillon Legatus 450 Aquila

      Available for purchase on AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Introducing AutoDrive! This cutting-edge, autonomous driving feature will take you to your chosen destination (i.e. job objective or placed pin on the map). If you have no set destination, it will take you on a leisurely ride through the streets of Night City. Simply hop in any of your vehicles, make sure you're on a road, and hold G (PC) / Left Stick (consoles) to activate. This feature is disabled when you enter combat or when your vehicle is heavily damaged.

    [/*]

  • Implemented Cinematic Camera for AutoDrive. Hold Q (PC) / D-Pad Right (consoles) to activate. Sit back and enjoy cinematic views of Night City as you cruise toward your destination.

    [/*]

  • Self-driving Delamain cabs are now available on demand! Simply open the menu to call vehicles, then select "Delamain Cab" from the list to request a ride. This feature unlocks after completing the job Don't Lose Your Mind (regardless of outcome) and receiving a message from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ is now available for vehicles from partner brands, including motorcycles. Additionally, the infamous hacker known as Cosmetic_Troll exploited a vulnerability and created a cracked version of Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ technology for lower-end vehicles. Please note, however, that some models do not support the technology, such as heavily modded nomad vehicles and job-related vehicles.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color schemes did not work properly on the Mizutani Shion MZ1 and MZ2.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color scheme could not be applied properly to the Villefort Deleon "Vindicator".

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Added 27 new NPCs that can be spawned in Photo Mode, including Rita Wheeler, the Cassel twins, fixers, Dum Dum, the iguana, Brendan, and more.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between alternative outfits for NPCs spawned in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between V's saved Wardrobe outfits in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • Added a confirmation pop-up when exiting Photo Mode to prevent accidental exits after setting up the perfect shot.

    [/*]

  • Added more customization options to the Look-At Camera feature, including an option for only the character's eyes to turn toward the camera instead of their entire body.

    [/*]

  • Added improvements to Lighting:

    • Lights now spawn around the camera instead of the player character.

      [/*]

    • Added an outline to the spotlight mesh and an indicator when it's off screen for better visibility.

      [/*]

    • Improved light movement speed on controllers.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Added multiple new stickers and frames, including iconic quotes and stylish overlays that let you turn your screenshots into Night City postcards – perfect for sharing memories from the City of Dreams.

    [/*]

  • Improved Depth of Field and moved it to the Camera tab.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Color Balance tab, allowing you to create your own custom filters.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Time and Weather tab:

    • Weather: includes rain, acid rain, fog, sandstorm, pollution, and sunny.

      [/*]

    • Time of Day: changes the time of day within Photo Mode.

      [/*]

    • Frame Forward: advances through an unlimited amount of frames to capture the perfect shot.

      [/*]

    • Game Speed: allows in-game time to progress while in Photo Mode."

      [/*]
    [/*]

Quality of Life & Accessibility

  • The game will now detect if the player is using inverted mouse button settings and automatically adjusts in-game button prompts accordingly.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to toggle aiming down sights in Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Jobs & Open World

  • Cyberpsycho Sighting: Bloody Ritual - the "Crack the ritualist's shard" objective now properly disappears from the Journal after completing the objective.

    [/*]

  • Sex on Wheels - now properly appears in the Journal after receiving the message from Jake Estevez.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where selecting a specific dialogue option in the conversation with Bree created a nameless, iconless item in the player's Inventory.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where the button to go to the lower level didn't appear on the elevator panel.

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where, when using a controller in Trauma Drama, the controllable character would default to shooting upwards instead of forward.

    [/*]

  • Players can now drop more Cyberware Capacity Shards if some within the intended drop limit were previously missed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing automatic weapons to fire slower than intended.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the Official BARGHEST Tac Vest didn't drop from the scripted Airdrop as intended.

    [/*]

  • The level 60 Engineer perk no longer activates the EMP blast outside of combat or after entering a vehicle.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to replay the gameplay tutorial at any time via Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Added an option to tell Johnny to go away after you look at him for a short while when he appears in the passenger seat. He takes the hint and disappears as a passenger for a couple days.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the sound of V's Radioport could be randomly interrupted by the Radioports of nearby NPCs.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where History by Gazelle Twin and Trash Generation played too loudly compared to other songs on the radio.

    [/*]

  • Improved the HDR Setting screen: fixed the HDR calibration preview so it correctly reflects the chosen settings, and clarified the description of the "Tone-Mapping Midpoint" setting.

    [/*]

  • Updated the End User Licence Agreement. You will be asked to accept it again when you load the game after updating.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several visual issues with missing, clipping, or floating textures.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several localization issues in various languages.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 4 for compatible AMD GPUs. IMPORTANT: The FSR 4 option will not be available in the in-game settings until the supporting AMD driver is installed. Please note that the driver will be released at a later date.

    [/*]

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution Frame Generation 3.1 for compatible hardware. It can now be used in combination with any upscaler.

    [/*]

  • Added support for ​Intel XeSS 2.0, with XeSS Frame Generation available on compatible hardware.

    [/*]

  • Added support for HDR10+ GAMING certified Intel GPUs. To enable this feature, your display must support the technology (find my display) and have "Game Mode" enabled. The HDR10+ GAMING toggle can be found in Settings in the Video tab.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the DLSS Super Resolution Preset would invisibly revert from the CNN model to the Transformer model after restarting the game, even though the UI still displayed the CNN model as active.

    [/*]

  • Added more detailed information to the DLSS Super Resolution Preset tooltip in Settings to help players choose the best option for their setup.

    [/*]

  • Added the ability to move the mouse cursor to a different display while in Windowed Borderless mode.

    [/*]

  • Increased the maximum save size from 12 MB to 15 MB.

    [/*]

  • It will now be possible to rebind the key used to jump out of vehicles with the Stuntjock perk.

    [/*]
